mechanics.text:
Core loop: the player spawns on the baseplate as an R6 character and sees a stationary target dummy a few studs ahead. Left-clicking (mouse button 1, ignored when the click is over UI) plays the attached R6 punch animation on the player's character. A punch counts as a hit when the dummy is within punch reach of the player's character during the swing. A simple on-screen counter goes up by exactly one for each hit.

Hit rule: the client sends a punch request to the server. The server validates it: the character is alive, the punch cooldown has elapsed, and the dummy is within roughly 6 studs and in front of the character. If the request is valid, the server registers one hit and updates that player's counter. Each swing can score at most one hit, and the player cannot start a new punch until the current animation finishes. A swing that misses plays the animation but does not change the counter.

Counter: a per-player HUD number, starting at 0, that increases by 1 on each valid hit and resets when the player rejoins. There is no win state, timer, health bar, score saving or other mechanic beyond what was asked.

Input: PC only, keyboard and mouse. Left click is the punch button. There are no touch, gamepad or console controls.

Exclusions: no sound effects and no visual effects on punch, hit or the counter. Any sounds or particle/visual effects embedded in the attached assets must be disabled or removed to honor this. The attached punch asset is retained as animation source data. The R6 rig is used only with a matching R6 animation.

Asset reuse: the attached Target Dummy (which contains scripts) and the attached punch animation model are used as selected. Inspect their included scripts and animation instances before writing any glue. Only the missing integration is authored: click input, hit validation and the counter.
assumptions: Reach is about 6 studs from the character's root part to the dummy, with the dummy roughly in front of the player.

The hit is registered when the swing starts, without waiting for a specific animation keyframe, and the swing cooldown equals the animation length. If the animation exposes a marker, the hit is timed to it.
A hit counts whether or not the dummy's own scripts react. The dummy's health and respawn behavior is kept only if it does not add visual or sound effects and does not interfere with the counter.
The counter is per player and not saved between sessions.
Click-and-hold does not auto-repeat. Each click is one punch.
The punch animation is played at normal action priority on the local player's R6 Animator.

No sounds, particles, flashes, camera shake or other feedback beyond the punch animation and the counter number changing.

assetsAndConfig.title: Punch the Dummy
assetsAndConfig.summary:
First minute: the player spawns near the origin on the gray baseplate. The Straw Target Dummy stands about 10 studs ahead at roughly (0,0,-10), facing spawn. A small dark panel in the top-left shows 'Hits' and '0'. The player walks to about 3-5 studs from the dummy and left-clicks. The attached R6 punch animation plays on their character. If the dummy is within about 6 studs of the character's root part and roughly in front, the server counts one hit and the HUD number goes up by exactly 1. A miss plays the animation but scores nothing. Holding the button does not repeat, and a new punch is only possible once the clip has finished. The reason to continue is simply to keep raising the counter. There is no win state, timer, health bar, saving, sound or visual effect.

Scene and script layout:
- Workspace/Forge_6e6ffc7fd435/World/TargetDummy is the imported dummy. It is anchored or otherwise stationary, stands on y=0 at about (0,0,-10) and faces spawn. Any embedded Sound, ParticleEmitter, Highlight or similar effect is disabled or removed. Its health and respawn behavior is kept only if it adds no sound or visual effect and does not interfere with the counter.
- ReplicatedStorage/Forge_6e6ffc7fd435/PunchConfig is a shared ModuleScript.
- ReplicatedStorage/Forge_6e6ffc7fd435/Remotes/PunchRequest is a RemoteEvent.
- ReplicatedStorage/Forge_6e6ffc7fd435/PunchAnimationSource holds the imported punch animation model as source data, not as a Workspace prop.
- ServerScriptService/Forge_6e6ffc7fd435/PunchService is a Script.
- StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/Forge_6e6ffc7fd435/PunchClient handles click input and animation. HitCounterHud in the same folder builds the ScreenGui with ResetOnSpawn=false.

Asset notes:
- Both attached assets were statically inspected with 0 scripts found. The dummy's search-hint constraint mentions 3 scripts, which contradicts the inspection. The build must re-inspect the real imported hierarchy.
- The punch model has about 2598 nodes and is probably one or more raw KeyframeSequences. If so, use RegisterKeyframeSequence for Studio playback, assign the returned ID unchanged to Animation.AnimationId, and record that publishing is a limitation. Confirm the clip is a punch and R6-compatible.
- Playback, clip length and hit feel remain unverified until native gameplay testing.

serverPunch.title: Punch the Dummy
serverPunch.summary:
First minute: the player spawns near the origin on the gray baseplate. The Straw Target Dummy stands about 10 studs ahead at roughly (0,0,-10), facing spawn. A small dark panel in the top-left shows 'Hits' and '0'. The player walks to about 3-5 studs from the dummy and left-clicks. The attached R6 punch animation plays on their character. If the dummy is within about 6 studs of the character's root part and roughly in front, the server counts one hit and the HUD number goes up by exactly 1. A miss plays the animation but scores nothing. Holding the button does not repeat, and a new punch is only possible once the clip has finished. The reason to continue is simply to keep raising the counter. There is no win state, timer, health bar, saving, sound or visual effect.

Scene and script layout:
- Workspace/Forge_6e6ffc7fd435/World/TargetDummy is the imported dummy. It is anchored or otherwise stationary, stands on y=0 at about (0,0,-10) and faces spawn. Any embedded Sound, ParticleEmitter, Highlight or similar effect is disabled or removed. Its health and respawn behavior is kept only if it adds no sound or visual effect and does not interfere with the counter.
- ReplicatedStorage/Forge_6e6ffc7fd435/PunchConfig is a shared ModuleScript.
- ReplicatedStorage/Forge_6e6ffc7fd435/Remotes/PunchRequest is a RemoteEvent.
- ReplicatedStorage/Forge_6e6ffc7fd435/PunchAnimationSource holds the imported punch animation model as source data, not as a Workspace prop.
- ServerScriptService/Forge_6e6ffc7fd435/PunchService is a Script.
- StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/Forge_6e6ffc7fd435/PunchClient handles click input and animation. HitCounterHud in the same folder builds the ScreenGui with ResetOnSpawn=false.

Asset notes:
- Both attached assets were statically inspected with 0 scripts found. The dummy's search-hint constraint mentions 3 scripts, which contradicts the inspection. The build must re-inspect the real imported hierarchy.
- The punch model has about 2598 nodes and is probably one or more raw KeyframeSequences. If so, use RegisterKeyframeSequence for Studio playback, assign the returned ID unchanged to Animation.AnimationId, and record that publishing is a limitation. Confirm the clip is a punch and R6-compatible.
- Playback, clip length and hit feel remain unverified until native gameplay testing.

serverPunch.visualDirection: Minimal training yard with no story. The existing gray baseplate, sky and lighting stay untouched, with no mood lighting and no lights added. The tan straw dummy is the only prop and the focal point, standing alone with open space around it. No fences, decorations, walls or platforms. The HUD is one compact panel in the top-left corner: a dark, semi-transparent background, a small 'Hits' label and a large high-contrast white number, sized for a PC screen and clear of the view of the dummy. The number changes instantly, with no tween, flash, sound or particle. The punch animation on the character is the only action feedback. Disable or remove any sound or visual effect embedded in the imported assets.

requirements.description: PunchService gives every player an integer 'Hits' attribute (name read from PunchConfig.HitsAttribute) set to 0 on PlayerAdded, before the character loads. It also covers players already in the game when the script starts. Only PunchService ever changes it, always by exactly +1 per valid hit. It is not saved and resets on rejoin. The service also does not reset it on respawn. The HUD reads it through the attribute, so the server sends no reply on the remote.
requirements.sourceQuote: a per-player HUD number, starting at 0, that increases by 1 on each valid hit and resets when the player rejoins
requirements.acceptance: On join, player:GetAttribute('Hits') is 0 (number, integer) before the character spawns. After N valid hits it equals N. It stays at its value across respawn and returns to 0 on a fresh join. A source scan finds no DataStore use and no other writer of the attribute.

requirements.description: Handle PunchConfig.RemoteName (ReplicatedStorage/Forge_6e6ffc7fd435/Remotes/PunchRequest) OnServerEvent. Ignore every payload argument. Resolve state only from the server side, using player.Character, its Humanoid and HumanoidRootPart. Reject the request if the character, Humanoid or HumanoidRootPart is missing, if Humanoid.Health <= 0, or if Workspace/Forge_6e6ffc7fd435/World/TargetDummy or its reference part (PrimaryPart, as recorded by worldLayout) is missing. Missing objects are handled with guarded lookups and no errors are thrown. Resolve the dummy at request time so a replaced model does not leave a stale reference. Use WaitForChild with sensible timeouts for the config and remote at startup.
requirements.sourceQuote: The server validates it: the character is alive, the punch cooldown has elapsed, and the dummy is within roughly 6 studs and in front of the character.
requirements.acceptance: A request from a dead player, from a player with no character, or while the dummy or its reference part is absent leaves Hits unchanged without a script error. A request that carries extra arguments (for example a fake distance or target) behaves identically to one with none. Nothing in the handler reads client-supplied values.

requirements.description: Count a hit only when the distance from HumanoidRootPart.Position to the dummy's reference part position is <= PunchConfig.Reach (6 studs) and the facing dot product is >= PunchConfig.MinFacingDot (0.3). The facing value is HumanoidRootPart.CFrame.LookVector dotted with the unit vector from the root part to the dummy. Read both numbers from PunchConfig with no hardcoded copies. Compute the direction safely when the distance is near zero.
requirements.sourceQuote: the dummy is within roughly 6 studs and in front of the character
requirements.acceptance: Punching from about 3-5 studs while facing the dummy adds 1. Punching from more than 6 studs away, or with the dummy behind the character, adds 0 but still plays the animation locally. Changing PunchConfig.Reach or MinFacingDot changes the server behavior with no edit to PunchService.

requirements.description: Track a per-UserId last-swing time with os.clock(). Reject a request until the swing cooldown (the punch clip length recorded in PunchConfig by assetsAndConfig, or PunchConfig.CooldownFallback only if the length is unavailable) has elapsed. A small documented network-jitter tolerance (no more than about 0.1 s) is allowed so a legitimate click made right after the client's track ends is not dropped. A request that passes the cooldown, hit or miss, consumes the swing, so a miss also starts the cooldown. A swing scores at most one hit. There is no auto-repeat or burst counting from spam. The hit is evaluated when the request arrives, which is swing start. If the clip inspection reported an animation marker, PunchConfig exposes its time and the reach and facing check is evaluated at that offset. Otherwise the check is immediate. No hit is invented.
requirements.sourceQuote: Keep these limits
requirements.acceptance: Two requests within one clip length from the same player add at most 1 in total. Rapid remote spam by an exploit cannot raise Hits faster than one per clip length. A miss followed by an immediate in-range request is still rejected until the cooldown elapses. Cooldowns for different players are independent. The report states the cooldown value and whether marker timing was used.

requirements.description: The hit is counted from the server's own geometry check only. It does not depend on the dummy's scripts, Humanoid health, damage, death or respawn reaction. PunchService never damages, moves, destroys or modifies the dummy, and never listens to dummy events to decide a hit. If the dummy respawns or is replaced, the next request resolves the current model and reference part.
requirements.sourceQuote: Keep these limits
requirements.acceptance: A valid punch counts identically whether the dummy has scripts, has a Humanoid, or has none. The dummy's Health and properties are unchanged by PunchService (source scan shows no TakeDamage, Health writes, Destroy or property writes on the dummy). After the dummy is removed and a replacement appears at the same path, hits count again.

requirements.description: Manage per-player state safely. Create the cooldown entry lazily or on PlayerAdded, and remove it and any connections on PlayerRemoving so no memory is retained for departed players. Handle respawn without stale references: resolve the character from player.Character on each request and do not cache it. A player who dies mid-cooldown is validated by the health check, and after respawn the cooldown table entry keeps working. Guard against the service starting after players already joined by iterating Players:GetPlayers(). Multiple simultaneous players each get an independent counter and cooldown.
requirements.sourceQuote: resets when the player rejoins
requirements.acceptance: After a player leaves, the internal per-UserId table has no entry for them. A respawned player can punch and score without any error. Two players punching in the same session each see only their own Hits value. No leaked connections remain after PlayerRemoving.

requirements.description: PunchService adds no sound, no visual effect and no reply feedback: no Sound, ParticleEmitter, Highlight, light, Explosion or camera effect, no RemoteEvent reply to the client, and no dummy reaction. The only observable server output of a hit is the Hits attribute changing by one.
requirements.sourceQuote: No sounds, particles, flashes, camera shake or other feedback beyond the punch animation and the counter number changing.
requirements.acceptance: A source scan of PunchService finds no Instance.new of sound or effect classes and no FireClient calls. Native play of a punch or hit shows and plays nothing from the server.

requirements.description: PunchService only reads the existing scene. It creates no floor, wall, platform, prop or light and does not touch Lighting, the spawn, or Workspace beyond reading Workspace/Forge_6e6ffc7fd435/World/TargetDummy. All lookups use one child name at a time (WaitForChild or FindFirstChild), never slash paths. The single script lives at ServerScriptService/Forge_6e6ffc7fd435/PunchService, with PC-only logic and no touch, gamepad or console handling.
requirements.sourceQuote: Use the existing baseplate (top at y=0) as the only ground. Do not add a floor, walls, ceiling or platforms, and do not change lighting, sky or atmosphere.
requirements.acceptance: After the service runs, Workspace, Lighting and the spawn are unchanged compared with the previous state. The script exists at the expected path, with the namespace preserved, and produces no infinite-yield warnings when all upstream objects exist.

requirements.description: PunchClient listens for left mouse button presses only (Enum.UserInputType.MouseButton1) through UserInputService.InputBegan. requirements.description: On an accepted click, play the imported R6 punch clip exactly once on the local character's Humanoid Animator. Use AnimationTrack.Priority = Enum.AnimationPriority.Action and Looped=false. Block any new punch while the track is playing or a swing is active, so the next punch is only possible once the clip has finished. Then fire the PunchRequest RemoteEvent (ReplicatedStorage/Forge_6e6ffc7fd435/Remotes/PunchRequest) with no arguments. Get the remote and PunchConfig through WaitForChild one child at a time. Do not send distances, targets or hit results.
requirements.sourceQuote: The punch animation is played at normal action priority on the local player's R6 Animator.
requirements.acceptance: Native play: a click plays the punch clip on the R6 character once. Clicks during the clip do nothing and fire no remote. The first click after the clip ends punches again. FireServer is called with zero arguments, and the source scan confirms the track priority is Action. Playback and feel are claimed only after native verification.

requirements.description: Resolve the playable punch Animation from ReplicatedStorage/Forge_6e6ffc7fd435/PunchAnimationSource according to the form that assetsAndConfig_importPunch recorded. If the chosen clip is a raw KeyframeSequence, call KeyframeSequenceProvider:RegisterKeyframeSequence, assign the returned ID unchanged to Animation.AnimationId (no hash:// prefix), and load it through Animator:LoadAnimation. If it is an existing Animation, use its AnimationId as-is. Use only the single chosen R6 punch clip, never an R15 clip. Never invent an AnimationId. If the source is missing or cannot be resolved, warn once, punch nothing and fire no remote, instead of substituting a tween or another clip. Report the publishing limitation for raw sequences honestly.
requirements.sourceQuote: Use the attached target dummy and the attached punch animation. Players use R6 characters.
requirements.acceptance: The resolver code path matches the source form recorded by the import task. The AnimationId comes from RegisterKeyframeSequence or the imported Animation, never a hard-coded guess. With the source removed, the client logs a warning and does not error or fire the remote. Native play confirms the clip loads on the R6 Animator. If playback cannot be tested, the gap is reported.

requirements.description: Handle the character lifecycle. Bind to LocalPlayer.CharacterAdded and to an already-present character at startup. On each new character wait for the Humanoid and its Animator, stop and destroy the previous AnimationTrack, and load a fresh track. Reset the swing state so a death mid-swing cannot lock punching after respawn. Disconnect every per-character connection (for example AnimationTrack.Stopped, marker signals, Humanoid.Died) and drop the old references on CharacterAdded and on character removal. Do not stack duplicate InputBegan connections across respawns: connect input once for the script lifetime. Do not punch while the Humanoid is dead.
requirements.sourceQuote: the character is alive, the punch cooldown has elapsed
requirements.acceptance: After several respawns, one click produces exactly one punch and one FireServer call, with no duplicated playback. No stale track from a previous character remains. A player who dies mid-swing can punch again on the new character. A source scan shows connections stored and disconnected on character change.

requirements.description: The client swing lock lasts as long as the clip: the track's Length as measured after loading, or PunchConfig.CooldownFallback only if the length cannot be read. It ends when the track stops. If the import inspection reported a KeyframeMarker or animation event for the punch, fire PunchRequest when that marker is reached (GetMarkerReachedSignal). Otherwise fire PunchRequest immediately at swing start, right after the track starts playing. Send at most one request per swing, whether the punch would hit or miss. Read numbers from PunchConfig with no hardcoded copies.
requirements.sourceQuote: Keep these limits
requirements.acceptance: The report states the swing lock value and whether marker timing was used. Exactly one remote fire happens per accepted click, and none while a swing is active. A click made just after the clip ends is not dropped by client logic. A source scan finds no hardcoded copy of the cooldown.

requirements.description: The client never inspects, damages, raycasts against or listens to the dummy. requirements.acceptance: A source scan of PunchClient finds no reference to TargetDummy, no Hits attribute writes and no hit computation. A click away from the dummy still plays the animation and fires the remote. The score changes only through the server-set attribute.

requirements.description: PunchClient and the animation loader add no sound, particle, highlight, light, camera shake, screen flash, tween, GUI feedback or other visual effect. requirements.description: Style the panel as a small, clean counter with high contrast. The panel Frame has a dark, semi-transparent background (for example near-black with BackgroundTransparency around 0.3-0.5) and modest rounded corners are acceptable. It holds a small TextLabel reading 'Hits' and a large TextLabel with the count, both in white text with a bold, readable font. The compact panel is about the size of a small counter in the corner, with padding and a UIListLayout or fixed positions, and it reads at a glance on a PC screen. The number's label is wide enough for multi-digit counts without clipping. The number changes only its Text. Adding no animation, tween, flash, color pulse or scale change is part of the style.
requirements.sourceQuote: The HUD is a small, clean counter in a screen corner, for example the label 'Hits' with a large number, with high-contrast white text on a dark semi-transparent panel so it reads at a glance.
requirements.acceptance: Native imagery shows a top-left dark semi-transparent panel with a small 'Hits' label and a large white number, legible against the baseplate scene. Values up to at least 4 digits fit without clipping. The panel is not oversized and does not cover the dummy.

requirements.description: The HUD adds no sound, particle, flash, highlight, camera change or visual effect. It uses no TweenService and no animated transitions, and no UIGradient or UIStroke animation. A count change is an instant text replacement with no visual acknowledgement beyond the number changing. The HUD creates no Sound instance and does not touch Lighting or the Camera.
requirements.sourceQuote: No sound effects and no visual effects.
requirements.acceptance: A source scan of HitCounterHud finds no TweenService, Instance.new of Sound, ParticleEmitter or Highlight, no Camera or Lighting access and no per-frame animation. Native play shows the number change instantly on a hit with nothing else happening.

requirements.description: The HUD is PC only for a keyboard and mouse player. It does not add touch buttons, tap wording, gamepad hints or a mobile layout. It creates no world objects and does not modify Workspace, Lighting, Sky, Atmosphere or the spawn. Its script lives only at StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/Forge_6e6ffc7fd435/HitCounterHud, and the only object it creates is the ScreenGui, parented to the LocalPlayer PlayerGui.
requirements.sourceQuote: PC only, keyboard and mouse.
requirements.acceptance: A source scan finds no Touch, Gamepad, VR or console handling, and no writes to Workspace or Lighting. Only one script is created, at the expected path, and it produces no infinite-yield warnings once PunchConfig exists.

requirements.description: Make the HUD robust across script restarts and player lifecycle. Before creating the ScreenGui, remove any stale ScreenGui with the same name from PlayerGui so a script restart cannot leave two counters. Store the attribute-changed connection and disconnect it if the ScreenGui is destroyed. Do not rebuild the HUD on CharacterAdded. Guard against a missing PlayerGui or PunchConfig with WaitForChild and sensible waits, so a slow load does not throw an error. The HUD does not stack duplicate connections.
requirements.acceptance: After a script restart or several respawns, PlayerGui holds exactly one HUD ScreenGui and exactly one attribute connection is active. Destroying the ScreenGui disconnects its connection. A source scan shows the connection stored and disconnected, and no CharacterAdded rebuild.

outline.title: Punch the Dummy
outline.summary:
First minute: the player spawns near the origin on the gray baseplate. The Straw Target Dummy stands about 10 studs ahead at roughly (0,0,-10), facing spawn. A small dark panel in the top-left shows 'Hits' and '0'. The player walks to about 3-5 studs from the dummy and left-clicks. The attached R6 punch animation plays on their character. If the dummy is within about 6 studs of the character's root part and roughly in front, the server counts one hit and the HUD number goes up by exactly 1. A miss plays the animation but scores nothing. Holding the button does not repeat, and a new punch is only possible once the clip has finished. The reason to continue is simply to keep raising the counter. There is no win state, timer, health bar, saving, sound or visual effect.

Scene and script layout:
- Workspace/Forge_6e6ffc7fd435/World/TargetDummy is the imported dummy. It is anchored or otherwise stationary, stands on y=0 at about (0,0,-10) and faces spawn. Any embedded Sound, ParticleEmitter, Highlight or similar effect is disabled or removed. Its health and respawn behavior is kept only if it adds no sound or visual effect and does not interfere with the counter.
- ReplicatedStorage/Forge_6e6ffc7fd435/PunchConfig is a shared ModuleScript.
- ReplicatedStorage/Forge_6e6ffc7fd435/Remotes/PunchRequest is a RemoteEvent.
- ReplicatedStorage/Forge_6e6ffc7fd435/PunchAnimationSource holds the imported punch animation model as source data, not as a Workspace prop.
- ServerScriptService/Forge_6e6ffc7fd435/PunchService is a Script.
- StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/Forge_6e6ffc7fd435/PunchClient handles click input and animation. HitCounterHud in the same folder builds the ScreenGui with ResetOnSpawn=false.

Asset notes:
- Both attached assets were statically inspected with 0 scripts found. The dummy's search-hint constraint mentions 3 scripts, which contradicts the inspection. The build must re-inspect the real imported hierarchy.
- The punch model has about 2598 nodes and is probably one or more raw KeyframeSequences. If so, use RegisterKeyframeSequence for Studio playback, assign the returned ID unchanged to Animation.AnimationId, and record that publishing is a limitation. Confirm the clip is a punch and R6-compatible.
- Playback, clip length and hit feel remain unverified until native gameplay testing.

Open conflict: a user message says 'Skip target dummy for now', but the approved proposal (revision 2) and asset choices still require the dummy. A game about punching a dummy has no target without it, so this plan keeps the approved dummy. The question below asks the user to confirm.
outline.visualDirection: Minimal training yard with no story. The existing gray baseplate, sky and lighting stay untouched, with no mood lighting and no lights added. The tan straw dummy is the only prop and the focal point, standing alone with open space around it. No fences, decorations, walls or platforms. The HUD is one compact panel in the top-left corner: a dark, semi-transparent background, a small 'Hits' label and a large high-contrast white number, sized for a PC screen and clear of the view of the dummy. The number changes instantly, with no tween, flash, sound or particle. The punch animation on the character is the only action feedback. Disable or remove any sound or visual effect embedded in the imported assets.

outline.sharedContracts:
Namespace Forge_6e6ffc7fd435.

Paths:
- ReplicatedStorage/Forge_6e6ffc7fd435/PunchConfig (ModuleScript)
- ReplicatedStorage/Forge_6e6ffc7fd435/Remotes/PunchRequest (RemoteEvent)
- ReplicatedStorage/Forge_6e6ffc7fd435/PunchAnimationSource
- Workspace/Forge_6e6ffc7fd435/World/TargetDummy
- ServerScriptService/Forge_6e6ffc7fd435/PunchService
- StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/Forge_6e6ffc7fd435/PunchClient and HitCounterHud

PunchConfig fields:
- Reach = 6 (studs, measured from HumanoidRootPart to the dummy's primary part)
- MinFacingDot = 0.3 (dummy must be roughly in front)
- HitsAttribute = 'Hits'
- RemoteName = 'PunchRequest'
- CooldownFallback: only if the clip length cannot be read; use the measured clip length

Remote contract: the client calls PunchRequest:FireServer() with no arguments. The server ignores any payload. It uses player.Character, the HumanoidRootPart CFrame and os.clock(). The server gives no reply. The score arrives via the attribute.

Counter state: the Player attribute 'Hits' is an integer set to 0 on PlayerAdded before the character loads. It is incremented only by PunchService, exactly +1 per valid hit and at most one per swing. It is not saved and it resets on rejoin. The HUD reads the attribute initially and via GetAttributeChangedSignal.

Server rules: reject if the character or Humanoid is missing or Health<=0, if the swing cooldown (equal to the clip length) has not elapsed for that UserId, or if the dummy or its primary part is missing. Count a hit only when the distance is <= Reach and the facing dot >= MinFacingDot. A miss does not change the counter but does consume the swing cooldown. Timing is at swing start, or at an animation marker if the clip exposes one. Clean the per-UserId state on PlayerRemoving.

Client rules: left mouse button only (MouseButton1, ignore gameProcessed clicks over UI). No auto-repeat on hold. Block a new punch while the track is playing. Play at Enum.AnimationPriority.Action on the R6 Humanoid Animator. Reload the track on CharacterAdded and disconnect old connections. No touch, gamepad or console bindings. No sound or visual effects anywhere. The HUD is a ScreenGui with ResetOnSpawn=false, created once. The number changes without a tween.

areas.title: Server punch validation and hit counter
areas.objective: Write PunchService. Initialize the 'Hits' attribute on each player. Handle PunchRequest with per-UserId cooldown derived from the clip length. Validate the character, health, reach (~6 studs) and facing. Add exactly one hit per valid swing that reaches the dummy, and count it regardless of the dummy's own scripts. Clean up state on PlayerRemoving and handle respawn. Add no sound or visual effects.

areas.title: Client left-click input and R6 punch animation
areas.objective: Write PunchClient. On a left click (not over UI, no hold-repeat, PC mouse only) and when not already swinging, play the imported R6 punch clip once on the local Animator at Action priority, then fire PunchRequest. Handle the animation source form found in inspection. Reload the track on respawn, disconnect stale connections, and never play an R15 animation.

areas.title: On-screen hit counter
areas.objective: Write HitCounterHud. Create one persistent ScreenGui (ResetOnSpawn=false) with a top-left dark semi-transparent panel, a 'Hits' label and a large white number. Read the 'Hits' attribute initially and update on change with no tween or effect. Keep it compact for PC and clear of the dummy.

areas.title: Native gameplay verification
areas.objective: In a protected review harness or native Studio play, verify: the imported assets are present at the expected paths; the dummy is visible and stationary at spawn; a left click plays the punch on the R6 character; a punch in range increments the counter by exactly 1; a punch out of range or behind the player does not; there is no auto-repeat or double count within one swing; there are no sounds or visual effects; the HUD shows 0 initially and after respawn; the state is cleaned up when the player leaves. Report anything that cannot be tested rather than claiming it passed.
